pairs.question: Itane tu ista credis?
pairs.derivation: Imagined objector's question and Augustine's own answer (diatribe/subiectio). Dropped the framing 'Dixerit aliquis:' ('someone may say:') as narration of the asking. 'ista' refers to the divine-parentage stories just discussed in section 3 (Aeneas son of Venus, Romulus son of Mars); the answer reuses the same 'ista', so the tight pair is self-contained ('Do you then believe these things?' / 'I for my part do not believe them'). Answer is the first sentence of the reply; cut before 'Nam et uir doctissimus eorum Varro...', which begins an extended discussion of Varro and is elaboration, not a direct answer.
